reason: The cell needs additional membrane as it grows, and phospholipids supply its bilayer.
expectation: The phospholipids will contribute to membrane growth.

alternatives.reason: Copying the genome is another clearly indicated goal.

effect: The phospholipids combined with new proteins to make membrane vesicles, completing the membrane goal and revealing a growth goal.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified that proteins were needed too.
reason: The nucleus contains opened DNA, and nucleotides are the building blocks needed to copy it.
expectation: The nucleotides will be used to copy the genome.

alternatives.reason: The vesicles may contribute to growing the cell surface.

effect: The genome is copied, with sister chromatids still joined; the copying goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction between copying the entire genome and making proteins is useful.
reason: The centrosomes organize microtubules, while tubulin and motors supply the spindle's components.
expectation: These components will form a chromosome-separating spindle.

alternatives.reason: The vesicles may help grow the cell's surface.

effect: The spindle is built, completing its goal and revealing the goal of making two daughter stem cells.
reaction: The picture makes clear that the spindle is ready but has not yet separated chromosomes.
reason: The new membrane vesicles can contribute to the growing cell's surface.
expectation: The vesicles will help enlarge the cell's surface and contents.

alternatives.reason: The spindle and copied genome must eventually work together to separate chromosomes.

effect: The vesicles fused with the cell surface, and continued production expanded its contents, completing the growth goal.
reaction: The before-and-after description usefully distinguishes growth from simply splitting the original cell.
reason: The copied chromosomes must interact with the spindle to be separated between daughter cells.
expectation: The spindle will engage the copied chromosomes for separation.

alternatives.reason: I could check how the grown cell participates in division.

effect: The spindle separated the sister chromatids into matching chromosome sets, but the cell still has shared cytoplasm.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and cell division is clear.
reason: Actin and myosin beneath the membrane could constrict the enlarged cell to divide its cytoplasm.
expectation: The actin and myosin will help the grown cell divide into two daughter cells.

alternatives.reason: The separated genomes also need to be incorporated into the daughter cells.

effect: Actin and myosin have no currently available combination, so I need to use the separated chromosomes and grown cell first.
reaction: The failed attempt was unexpected given their apparent role in dividing the cytoplasm.
reason: The separated chromosome sets and enlarged cell body are the remaining complementary parts of the division process.
expectation: Combining these will advance division toward two daughter cells with complete genomes.

effect: The separated chromosome sets are now enclosed in two daughter nuclei within one shared cytoplasm.
reaction: The intermediate stage explains why dividing the cytoplasm comes next.
reason: Cortical actin and myosin can now constrict the cell containing both daughter nuclei.

choice.with: Stem cell with two daughter nuclei

expectation: The cell will divide its cytoplasm to produce two daughter stem cells.

effect: Actin and myosin divided the shared cytoplasm, producing two unspecialized daughter stem cells and completing the final goal.
reaction: The separate daughter cells are a satisfying conclusion to the staged division.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the chromosome sets was most worthwhile: the planned illustration and explanation distinguish chromosome separation from division of the shared cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed actin-and-myosin attempt was the least worthwhile moment. Its role in constriction was apparent, but the need to form daughter nuclei first was not yet clear.

surprise.text: Phospholipids did not combine directly with the cell; compatibility feedback instead led to membrane vesicles made with new proteins.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to form two daughter nuclei before actin and myosin could be used felt somewhat arbitrary at the time, although the intermediate made the sequence clearer afterward.

continue.text: I would continue: the constructions connected genome copying, growth and division clearly, and the final description suggests descendants can take different paths.
